Understanding pedagogical challenges faced by technology teachers in special needs classrooms
abstract: <jats:p>Teaching learners with special educational needs requires dynamic and adaptive pedagogical strategies that can lead to social development and academic success. This can be possible if teachers are assisted in mitigating the daily challenges of teaching such learners. This qualitative exploratory case study investigated the pedagogical challenges encountered by two Grade 9 Technology teachers in the Capricorn District of Limpopo Province. This study used Shulman’s Content and Pedagogical Knowledge framework to understand teachers’ challenges. Data was collected through semi-structured interviews and classroom observations; all collected data were analysed thematically. This study found that teachers experienced various challenges, including the emotional labour of teaching, burnout in the LSEN environment and the enactment of instructional knowledge. The study concluded that the sampled teachers displayed weaknesses in lesson planning, activating learners’ prior knowledge, diagnosing errors, achieving curriculum objectives and sustaining engagement. As a result, it was recommended that support through teacher assistants, creative differentiated strategies and enhanced digital-technology literacy to improve outcomes for learners with special needs was imminent.</jats:p>
venue: Journal of Education and Learning Technology

Integration of Biomechanics and Digital Technology: Using Kinovea for Motion Analysis and Learning for Beginner Athletes
abstract:
<jats:p>Background: The integration of biomechanics with digital motion-analysis technologies has introduced new approaches for examining movement efficiency, kinematic characteristics, and technical patterns in walking and running activities. Kinovea, as an accessible motion-analysis software, provides both visual and quantitative feedback. However, its application in supporting technique development among beginner athletes remains insufficiently explored.
Aim: This study aims to describe the use of Kinovea in biomechanics training and examine its contribution to the awareness of kinematic characteristics and movement techniques among beginner athletes.
Methods: A descriptive qualitative design involved 72 beginner athletes aged 18–25 years selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected over 16 weeks through interviews, field observations, and motion video recordings analyzed using Kinovea. Kinematic data focused on joint angles, stride behavior, and movement phases during walking, running, and the flight phase. Qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis with NVivo 12, while kinematic results were interpreted descriptively to identify performance patterns and areas for technical refinement.
Result: Kinematic analysis showed coordinated joint-angle patterns across all phases. Walking analysis identified arm swing angles of 50.9°–58.8° and leg separation angles of 64.3°–67.2°, indicating a stable gait rhythm. The running analysis revealed knee angles of 68.8°–69.8° and elbow angles of 87.6°–89.1°, indicating efficient propulsive mechanics. The flight phase demonstrated knee angles of 81.2°–87.8° and elbow angles of 80.4°–88.3°, suggesting effective momentum use and postural stability. These measurements supported stride-efficiency assessment and technique evaluation. Qualitative findings revealed that Kinovea enabled athletes to interpret movement phases and identify technical inefficiencies through slow-motion and frame-by-frame visualization.
Conclusion: Kinovea supports basic motion analysis by providing clear kinematic information and helping beginner athletes observe and refine their movement techniques. The findings also offer practical value for coaches by enabling more precise identification of inefficient patterns and guiding targeted corrections during early-stage training.</jats:p>
venue: Journal of Coaching and Sports Science

HYBRID NETWORK INTRUSION DETECTION SYSTEM BASED ON SIGNATURE ANALYSIS AND MACHINE LEARNING METHODS
abstract: <jats:p>In the context of increasing complexity of modern network infrastructures and the growing number of cyberattacks, improving the effectiveness of intrusion detection systems is a highly relevant task. The aim of this work is to develop and investigate a hybrid approach to network attack detection based on a combination of signature-based analysis and intelligent machine learning methods.  The research methods include analysis of requirements for anomaly detection systems, comparative analysis of existing solutions, design of a hybrid system architecture, and experimental modeling using multiclass classification of network traffic. The results demonstrate that integrating a neural model with a traditional detection system improves attack detection coverage and reduces the number of false positives.  The practical significance of the study lies in the possibility of deploying the proposed architecture in real corporate networks, while the theoretical significance consists in substantiating the effectiveness of a hybrid approach to traffic analysis. Future research directions include adaptive model training and expansion of the range of detectable attacks.</jats:p>

Transforming Education through Technology: The Case of COVID 19 Digital Learning in Nagaland
abstract:
<jats:p>Through the perspective of the COVID-19 pandemic and the disruption and opportunity it engendered, this chapter follows a transformative effect of EdTech and Digital education in India particularly in Nagaland through analysis. Drawing upon national policy frameworks, conceptual literature on educational technology, and contextual evidence based on the case of Nagaland, the chapter considers the rapid migration to digital learning as an emergency strategy (in response to the ongoing institution closures) based on the stark shifts in pedagogical practice, access to education services, and preparedness. The findings show that, including the ability of national programmes such as NEP 2020, SWAYAM, DIKSHA, PM e-VIDYA, and others, to promote access to digital tools was low within periphery or hill areas (e.g., Nagaland), due to lack of infrastructural resources, digital divide, unprepared teachers and economic/social divides, and more. The pandemic exposed the deep social and infrastructure divides in connectivity, device availability, assessment and learner engagement, with implications that were especially grave in rural and tribal settings. Although it accelerated the pace of innovation and the application of blended and low-tech learning practices teachers have been experimenting with digital platforms and the post-COVID recovery process, including remedial programmes and hybrid instruction. The chapter also discusses that blended learning is the most fitting, viable and sustainable approach for reaching the technological level in the field of educational technology at Nagaland. It implies that technology-mediated education can improve equity, quality, and resilience, but only under the conditions of inclusive policy design, strong digital infrastructure, vigorous teacher capability building, and culturally appropriate digital content.
Keywords: Educational technology, digital learning, COVID-19, Nagaland, online education, Challenges, blended learning</jats:p>

title: The Nexus of Leadership and Learning: Exploring Female Principals' Influence on the Teaching-Learning Process in Secondary Schools
abstract: <jats:p>The research paper will set out to debate the role played by the leadership competencies of principals in the teaching and learning process. The research will embrace a quantitative research design that will seek to answer the question concerning the relationship that exists between leadership skills of possessed by the  principals and the ongoing teaching-learning process in the female secondary schools using a co-relational study design. A survey instrument comprising of 37 items, which measured the leadership skills possessed by the selected principals and the prevailing teaching learning process, was used in the collection of data. Questionnaires for this study were administered to 108 male and female educators who were serving in secondary schools in Tehsil Wari, upper Dir and among them 100 questionnaires were submitted and were deemed to be useful in the analysis. The data in hand were calculated using Statistical Package of the Social Sciences (SPSS) version-27 and the obtained results indicated that the collected data was normally distributed. The findings revealed that all the variables of the study had great correlations. The analysis of the data was done through linear regression to measure the effect that the leadership skills of the principals had on the teaching learning process and this indicated that leadership skills of the principals have statistically significant effect on the teaching learning process. The policies derived out of this research can be a good guide to both the policymakers and organizational leaders because they can provide a good outline on how to empower the leaders in charge of the principals and as well as exert more influence on the effective teaching and learning processes.</jats:p>
ai_summary: Research paper will debate role played by principals in teaching and learning process . Research will embrace a quantitative research design that will seek to answer the question about the relationship between leadership skills of principals and teaching-learning process .

title: Cyber Defense Digital Twins: A Federated Learning and Zero-Trust AI Architecture for Autonomous Threat Prediction and Response
abstract: <jats:p>Modern enterprise networks operate under persistent threats that exploit cloud-native misconfigurations, identity sprawl, and API vulnerabilities at machine speed. Existing security operations center (SOC) architectures remain largely reactive, signature-dependent, and incapable of predicting multi-stage lateral movement. This paper proposes the Cognitive Cyber Defense Digital Twin (CCDT), a unified architecture integrating federated learning (FL), graph neural network (GNN)-based attack-path forecasting, adversarially hardened detection models, and autonomous Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR) with deception engineering. The CCDT constructs a continuously synchronized digital replica of organizational assets and employs reinforcement learning-based red agents to stress-test detection models. A federated intelligence mesh enables cross-organizational privacy-preserving gradient sharing. Experimental evaluations against CICIDS-2018 and LANL datasets demonstrate 52% faster attack-path detection, 41% reduction in false positive rate, and 60% reduction in mean-time-to-respond (MTTR) compared to traditional SOC baselines. Integrated Explainable AI (XAI) modules using SHAP values enable audit-ready compliance reporting. The CCDT represents a paradigm shift from reactive monitoring to predictive, autonomous, and privacy-preserving cyber defense for hybrid cloud environments.</jats:p>
venue: International Journal of Scientific Research in Computer Science, Engineering and Information Technology

Dual-Interface Engineering of Cs2CuBiBr6-Based Memristive Synaptic Devices for Neuromorphic Computing.
abstract: Pb-free double perovskite Cs2CuBiBr6 (CCBB)-based resistive random-access memory (ReRAM) synaptic devices are developed using a dual-interface engineering approach to achieve stable resistive switching and neuromorphic functionality. High-quality CCBB thin films are obtained via optimized antisolvent-assisted crystallization, enabling enhanced crystallinity and reduced defect-induced energetic disorder. Modification of the bottom interface with a poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) polystyrene sulfonate (PEDOT:PSS) interlayer improves CCBB film continuity and provides a more favorable environment for homogeneous charge injection. The introduction of an ultrathin bathocuproine (BCP) interlayer at the top interface regulates the spatial redistribution of Ag-related species. The cooperative regulation of charge injection and Ag-related electro-ionic processes promotes more reproducible formation and rupture of localized conductive pathways, resulting in improved switching stability and device-to-device reproducibility. The CCBB-based ReRAM exhibits reliable bipolar resistive switching over 600 cycles, an on/off current ratio of approximately 103, and stable data retention up to 104 s. Gradual and repeatable conductance modulation under electrical pulse stimulation further demonstrates synaptic potentiation and depression behaviors. MNIST-based neural network simulations reveal excellent neuromorphic performance, with up to 90% recognition accuracy. This work highlights cooperative dual-interface regulation of charge injection and Ag-related electro-ionic processes as an effective design strategy for achieving reliable Pb-free perovskite ReRAM and neuromorphic synaptic operation.

title: Digital image analysis-based quantification of p53 immunohistochemistry in gastric cancer: a systematic comparison of three-tier cutoff-derivation strategies in tissue microarrays.
abstract: p53 immunohistochemistry (IHC) is a common surrogate for TP53 alteration, but in gastric cancer, its concordance is imperfect and depends on a non-standardized cutoff. Digital pathology enables H-score quantification, yet neither its reproducibility nor the choice of cutoff- derivation strategy has been systematically compared. A semi-automated digital workflow quantified p53 IHC in tissue microarrays from 528 gastric cancer patients. Tumor cells were detected with a deep-learning model (InstanSeg), and nuclear staining was expressed as a continuous H-score (0-300). Reproducibility was assessed at each observer-dependent step. Five thresholding strategies were compared: manual cutoffs, tertiles, log-rank optimization, the extended Youden index, and volume under the receiver operating characteristic surface (VUS). The latter two strategies used the manual three-tier IHC interpretation as the reference standard. Quantification was reproducible: two independent manual interpretations agreed in 91.7% of cores (κ = 0.845). The H-score was robust to the detection algorithm (intraclass correlation coefficient, 0.990) and to repeated threshold determination (0.954). H-scores were right-skewed (median, 45.5), and the strategies yielded distinct cutoffs (8.0-27.6 and 78.6-106.0). Log-rank optimization provided the widest separation but lost significance after multiplicity adjustment (p = .168). The extended Youden and VUS cutoffs were statistically indistinguishable. As a supporting check, all classifications showed nominal overall-survival separation, with low and overexpression faring similarly worse than wild-type. Digital p53 IHC quantification was reproducible at each observer-dependent step. The extended Youden and VUS criteria performed equivalently; therefore, we propose Youden as a reasonable default, pending validation and TP53 correlation.

title: Retrospective multi-reader evaluation of a Deep-Learning-based cancer detection model in Contrast-Enhanced Mammography.
abstract: To evaluate the clinical impact of a deep-learning-based computer-aided diagnostic tool applied to contrast-enhanced mammography on radiologists' diagnostic accuracy and reading efficiency. In this retrospective single-centre study, 150 contrast-enhanced mammography examinations were interpreted by five radiologists. Each case was read and annotated twice in two sequential sessions: first without assistance and then with the computer-aided diagnostic tool, with a minimum 4-week washout period. Diagnostic performance was assessed at lesion and breast levels using free-response receiver operating characteristic analysis, area under the curve, and false-positive rate. Reading time for one radiologist was recorded as an exploratory measure. The computer-aided diagnostic tool was associated with improved lesion-level performance for most radiologists, with a mean increase in the area under the free-response curve of 0.030 ± 0.018. At 89% sensitivity, false-positive findings decreased by an average of 11.4% ± 24% across all radiologists. No improvement was observed at the breast level, possibly related to the tool's single-view analysis and dataset characteristics. An exploratory analysis showed a 31% reduction in reading time for one radiologist. Integration of a deep learning-based computer-aided diagnostic tool into contrast-enhanced mammography was associated with improved lesion-level diagnostic performance and reduced false-positive findings, without measurable improvement at the breast level. To our knowledge, this study provides one of the early clinical evaluations of a deep learning-based computer-aided diagnostic tool for contrast-enhanced mammography, suggesting potential improvements in lesion-level diagnostic performance and workflow efficiency while highlighting current limitations at the breast level.
ai_summary: 150 mammography examinations were interpreted by five radiologists . Each case was read and annotated twice in two sequential sessions . The computer-aided diagnostic tool was associated with improved lesion-level performance for most radiologists.

title: MRI-Based Machine Learning to Differentiate True Progression from Pseudoprogression in Glioblastoma: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Differentiating true progression (TP) from pseudoprogression (PsP) after chemoradiation for glioblastoma remains clinically difficult. We evaluated externally validated diagnostic performance of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based machine learning models and appraised study quality and transparency. PubMed, Embase, MEDLINE, and Cochrane Library were searched through October 1, 2025 (PROSPERO registration CRD420251144894). Eligible adult glioblastoma studies used MRI-based machine learning to distinguish TP from PsP against histopathology and/or clinicoradiologic follow-up. The primary meta-analysis included external test cohorts with extractable 2 × 2 data; internal and combined internal and external test analyses were secondary. Diagnostic accuracy was synthesized with bivariate random-effects models. Thirty-one studies including 2,344 patients undergoing imaging assessment were included. Seven external test cohorts, including 219 patient observations, entered the primary meta-analysis. Pooled sensitivity was 0.78 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.63-0.88), specificity was 0.75 (95% CI, 0.63-0.84), and summary area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was 0.81 (bootstrap 95% CI, 0.69-0.91). Internal test cohorts showed higher apparent performance than external cohorts (AUC, 0.91 vs 0.81), but the difference was not statistically significant (difference, -0.09; 95% CI, -0.22 to 0.02; P = 0.12). Risk of bias was frequently high or unclear, and reporting transparency was heterogeneous. MRI-based machine learning showed moderate-to-good external validation performance for TP-versus-PsP discrimination, but evidence remains limited by small external test cohorts, bias, and incomplete reporting. Larger transparent multicenter validations are needed before routine clinical implementation. Following chemoradiation for glioblastoma, new or worsening MRI abnormalities may represent either true tumor progression or pseudoprogression. This review evaluated machine learning studies for distinguishing true progression from pseudoprogression, emphasizing models tested at external centers. External validation showed moderate-to-good diagnostic performance, but the evidence was limited by small test cohorts, inconsistent reference standards, and incomplete reporting. Larger multicenter studies using current WHO 2021 molecular definitions, standardized diagnostic criteria, and complete reporting are needed before these models can be used routinely in clinical practice.
ai_summary: The study used MRI-based machine learning to distinguish TP from PsP against histopathology and/or clinicoradiologic follow-up . The primary meta-analysis included external test cohorts with extractable 2 × 2 data .

title: Comorbidity patterns and sex differences in late-onset Alzheimer's disease using electronic records.
abstract: In this retrospective study, we applied unsupervised learning techniques to electronic medical records from the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF) to characterize Alzheimer's disease (AD) comorbidity patterns. Given the well-known female predominance in AD, we performed sex-stratified analyses to explore differences in comorbidity patterns based on sex. Findings were evaluated using an independent UC-wide dataset. Among 8,363 patients in the UCSF dataset, we observed five data-driven comorbidity clusters related to cardiovascular conditions, gastrointestinal disorders, and frailty-related conditions such as pneumonia and pressure ulcers, as well as groups with higher and lower overall comorbidity burden. Sex-stratified analyses within clusters identified variation in comorbidity patterns, including circulatory diseases in males in cluster 2 and bladder stones in females in cluster 3. Key results demonstrate partial consistency in the UC-wide dataset. Our study provides a structured characterization of comorbidity heterogeneity in AD and highlights sex-related differences, though findings should be interpreted as descriptive and hypothesis-generating.
ai_summary: Study used unsupervised learning techniques to characterize Alzheimer's disease (AD) comorbidity patterns . Sex-stratified analyses identified variation in comor bidity patterns, including circulatory diseases in males in cluster 2 and bladder stones in females in cluster 3 .

title: Prevalence of SARS-COV-2 infection, Relationship between SARS-CoV-2 and HIV among Sex Workers in Cotonou.
abstract: Since the outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic, few studies have been carried out on the prevalence of the severe acute respiratory syndrome of the coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), particularly in groups of patients with comorbidity factors. Moreover, the question of whether HIV increases the risk of contracting SARS-COV-2 or its severity has been the subject of some research. To determine the prevalence of SARS-COV-2 and estabilish the relationship between HIV infection and SARS-CoV-2 infection in female sex workers. Descriptive cross-sectional study of female sex workers attending the Racine clinic in Cotonou, Benin. Statistical data entry and analysis were performed using Excel and Stata 15 software. Proportions, means and frequencies with standard deviation were estimated and compared by chi2 and Fisher tests at the significance level of 5%. A total of 259 sex workers were recruited for this study, with a mean age of 34.28 ± 9.83 years, ranging from 18 to 70 years. The overall occurrence of SARS-CoV-2 among female sex workers reported in our study was 81.5%. Those of HIV and co-infection HIV SARS-COV 2 were 19.7% and 13.5% respectively. HIV-infected sex workers had a significantly lower risk of SARS-CoV-2 infection (OR=0.39 with 95% CI [0.19-0.80] and p=0.010), while TCD4+ lymphocyte count ≥ 500 was not significantly associated with a risk of SARS-CoV-2 infection (OR=0.40 with 95% CI [0.11-1.36] and p=0.142). This study shows that the prevalence of SARS-CoV-2 infection among sex workers is high. Sex workers who are infected with HIV are significantly less likely to be infected with SARS-CoV-2. Depuis le début de la pandémie de COVID-19, peu d'études ont été menées sur la prévalence du syndrome respiratoire aigu sévère dû au coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), en particulier dans les groupes de patients présentant des facteurs de comorbidité. Par ailleurs, la question de savoir si le VIH augmente le risque de contracter le SARS-CoV-2 ou d'en aggraver la sévérité a fait l'objet de certaines recherches. Déterminer la prévalence du SARS-CoV-2 et établir la relation entre l'infection par le VIH et l'infection par le SARS-CoV-2 chez les travailleuses du sexe. Étude transversale descriptive menée auprès des travailleuses du sexe fréquentant la clinique Racine à Cotonou, Bénin. La saisie et l'analyse des données statistiques ont été réalisées avec les logiciels Excel et Stata 15. Les proportions, moyennes et fréquences avec écart-type ont été estimées et comparées à l'aide des tests du chi² et de Fisher, avec un seuil de signification fixé à 5 %. Au total, 259 travailleuses du sexe ont été recrutées pour cette étude, avec un âge moyen de 34,28 ± 9,83 ans (plage : 18 à 70 ans). La prévalence globale du SARS-CoV-2 rapportée dans notre étude était de 81,5 %. Celle du VIH et de la co-infection VIH/SARS-CoV-2 étaient respectivement de 19,7 % et 13,5 %. Les travailleuses du sexe infectées par le VIH présentaient un risque significativement plus faible d'infection par le SARS-CoV-2 (OR = 0,39 ; IC 95 % [0,19-0,80] ; p = 0,010), tandis que le taux de lymphocytes TCD4+ ≥ 500 n'était pas significativement associé au risque d'infection par le SARS-CoV-2 (OR = 0,40 ; IC 95 % [0,11-1,36] ; p = 0,142). Cette étude montre que la prévalence de l'infection par le SARS-CoV-2 chez les travailleuses du sexe est élevée. title: Text-based nutrient estimation by large language models: a comparative evaluation against the Chinese Food Composition Table.
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly provide nutrient information, but their accuracy for Chinese foods and their consistency across repeated queries are not well established. To compare nutrient estimates from nine general-purpose LLMs with the Chinese Food Composition Table (CFCT) and assess within-model reproducibility. For 299 commonly consumed Chinese foods, each model estimated energy and 14 nutrients per 100 g in three independent runs (8,073 food-level outputs). Model means were compared with CFCT values using absolute-agreement intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs), bias, mean absolute error (MAE), root mean squared error, percentage error, and Bland-Altman limits of agreement. Repeated-run ICCs and coefficients of variation assessed reproducibility. Agreement was excellent for energy, fat, carbohydrate, sodium, and vitamin C across all nine models, and good to excellent for protein. Performance was less consistent for vitamin A, zinc, iron, and potassium. Repeated-run stability was high for energy and macronutrients but lowest for vitamin A. GLM had the most favorable combined accuracy-stability profile, followed by Minimax and Qwen. Even when aggregate agreement was high, individual food estimates sometimes showed substantial error. General-purpose LLMs can approximate energy and macronutrient values for Chinese foods under controlled text-based conditions, but micronutrient estimates remain less dependable. Values intended for clinical or other high-stakes applications should be verified using validated food-composition resources and, where appropriate, qualified nutrition professionals.

title: A primary care-oriented framework for osteoporosis prediction: integrating multi-algorithm feature selection and machine learning model benchmarking.
abstract: Large-scale screening and primary care diagnosis of osteoporosis are challenging due to the limited availability of dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA). Therefore, predictive models for osteoporosis that do not rely on bone mineral density measurements are essential. Using routine health examination data and applying a consensus feature selection strategy, we constructed machine learning (ML)-based models and compared their performance across multiple dimensions. To develop a robust, low-cost, and interpretable framework for osteoporosis prediction based on readily available information, which can be easily integrated into electronic health systems to inform DXA referral in resource-limited settings. Variables covered by the basic health examination package were obtained from participants who underwent health examinations between January 2024 and January 2025. We implemented a strategy in which only features selected by at least four out of the seven feature selection methods were retained. Six ML algorithms were employed to develop models, and their prediction performances were compared across discrimination, goodness-of-fit, and clinical utility. A total of 2,260 participants were included, with an osteoporosis prevalence of 7.1%. Eight features: age, sex, body mass index, alkaline phosphatase, hematocrit, high-density lipoprotein, urea, and platelet count, were selected for model development. In the validation set, the random forest and artificial neural network (ANN) models demonstrated strongest screening performance, with AUCs of 0.895 (95% CI 0.867-0.923) and 0.890 (95% CI 0.862-0.919), respectively. The ANN model additionally exhibited superior calibration. Shapley additive explanations were applied to interpret the ANN model for osteoporosis prediction. This study presents an easily integrable model for osteoporosis prediction based on routine health examination data. The ANN model provides robust prediction, offering a potential tool for pre-DXA triage and early identification of high-risk individuals in primary care and resource-limited settings.
